code.title: Recursive Sum to N
code.description:
A maths mentor app builds a warm-up drill where the running total of all points from 1 to N is produced by a function that calls itself with N-1 until it reaches 0. Read N and print the recursive total. The core logic must use recursion, not loops.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Sum 1..N is <total>

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 1000

code.title: Recursive Factorial Finder
code.description:
A chemistry lab counts possible arrangements of sample trays and needs factorials computed by recursion: N! = N * (N-1)!, stopping at 0! = 1. Read N and print N! using a function that calls itself.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Factorial of <N> is <result>

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 15

code.title: Recursive Descending List
code.description:
A launchpad test bench prints its test indices in reverse order as a recursion warm-up. Read N and print the numbers from N down to 1 on a single line separated by single spaces, using a recursive function.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
One line with N, N-1, ..., 1 separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000

code.title: Rocket Countdown Liftoff
code.description:
A college space club simulator fires a rocket with a recursive countdown: each call prints its own count and then calls itself with one less, until the base case prints the launch call. Read the starting count N and print the countdown.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
One number per line from N down to 1, then the line Liftoff!

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 30

code.title: Recursive Power of X
code.description:
An embedded systems lab computes sensor scaling factors x^n with a recursive power function that multiplies the base n times and returns 1 when the exponent hits 0. Read the base and the exponent.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: base x and exponent n.

Output Format:
Power result: <x^n>

Constraints:
1 <= x <= 9, 0 <= n <= 15

code.title: Recursive Digit Counter
code.description:
A water meter portal counts how many digits a reading contains using recursion: each call strips the last digit and adds 1, and any single-digit number (including 0) counts as 1 digit. Read N and print the count.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Digit count: <c>

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 1000000

code.title: Backup Folder Size Sum
code.description:
A backup tool inspects a folder holding N files and totals their sizes recursively: every call reads one size into the running total and then recurses on the rest. Read N and then N sizes, and print the folder report.

Input Format:
First line: N. Second line: N integers (sizes in MB).

Output Format:
Files: <N>
Total size: <total> MB

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= each size <= 5000

code.title: Committee Approval Chain
code.description:
A student committee passes a budget request upward through N approval levels: the recursive call dives to level 0 first, and each level then records its approval as the stack unwinds, so the approvals appear from level 1 up to level N. Read N and simulate the chain.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Approval chain started
Level 1 approved
Level 2 approved
...
Level <N> approved
Final decision recorded

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 10

code.description:
A build server runs a dependency chain: subtask N needs subtask N-1 finished first, and subtask 1 has no dependency. A recursive function prints Subtask k started before diving into k-1 and prints Subtask k done after that call returns, then the parent line closes the trace. Read N and print the full trace.

One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Subtask <N> started down to Subtask 1 started, then Subtask 1 done up to Subtask <N> done, then the line Main task complete (one started line and one done line per subtask).

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 30

code.title: Fibonacci Worksheet Generator
code.description:
A maths tutor app builds a practice worksheet with the first K Fibonacci numbers (starting 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, ...). Every term must come from a recursive fib function and the series must be printed by a recursive printer, so no loops are allowed anywhere.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: K.

Output Format:
Fibonacci series: <first K terms separated by single spaces>
Terms printed: <K>

Constraints:
1 <= K <= 25

code.title: Plank Cutting GCD
code.description:
A carpentry workshop cuts two plank lengths into the largest identical tiles with zero waste: that tile size is the greatest common divisor of the two lengths, found with the recursive Euclid method gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b) until b becomes 0. Read the two lengths and print the tile size.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: length A and length B.

Output Format:
Tile size: <gcd> cm

Constraints:
1 <= A, B <= 100000

code.title: Vanity Number Analyzer
code.description:
A car showroom's vanity number desk analyses a customer's favourite number with two recursive functions: one sums the digits (peeling one digit per call) and one builds the mirror form of the number. Read N and print both results.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Digit sum: <sum>
Mirror number: <reversed digits as an integer>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 999999. The mirror is built as an integer, so trailing zeros of N disappear (e.g. 120 mirrors to 21).

code.title: Palindrome Plate Checker
code.description:
A regional transport office checks whether a proposed registration plate reads the same in both directions. A recursive checker compares the outermost characters and moves both ends inward until they cross. Read the plate (a single word) and report the verdict.

Input Format:
One line with one word: the plate text.

Output Format:
Palindrome: Yes
or
Palindrome: No

Constraints:
1 <= plate length <= 100. The comparison is case sensitive, so Anna is not a palindrome.
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= plate length <= 100, comparison is case sensitive

code.title: Parcel Weight Totaler
code.description:
A courier drone scans N parcels and builds its load report with recursion: one recursive pass reads the weights into an array, one computes the total weight, and one carries the heaviest weight up the call stack. Read N and the weights, then print the report.

Input Format:
First line: N. Second line: N integers (weights in kg).

Output Format:
Parcels: <N>
Total weight: <sum> kg
Heaviest parcel: <max> kg

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 500, 0 <= each weight <= 500. With N = 0 both the total and the heaviest value are 0.

A tile showroom prints an area report using an inline helper: inline long long square(long long side) returns side * side, and the report calls it twice, once per tile and once inside the grand total. Read the tile side S and the number of tiles T, then print the report.

One line with two integers: tile side S and tiles ordered T.

Output Format:
Tile side: <S> cm
Tile area: <S*S> sq cm
Tiles ordered: <T>
Total area: <S*S*T> sq cm

Constraints:
1 <= S <= 100, 1 <= T <= 1000

Output Format:

Minimum moves: <2^N - 1>
Move disk <k> from <peg> to <peg>   (one line per move, in order)
All disks stacked on peg C

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 4. With N = 0 there are no moves and only the opening lines and the final line print.

Level 2 payout:

Top payout:

code.description:
A security keypad merges two access codes by interleaving their digits alternately from the left: one digit from code A, then one from code B, repeating; when one code runs out, the remaining digits of the other code are appended in order. The merge is built recursively on the code strings and the merged digit sum is computed recursively too. Read the two codes and print the report.

One line with two integers: code A and code B.

Output Format:
Code A: <A>
Code B: <B>
Merged code: <merged digits>
Merged length: <len>
Merged digit sum: <sum>

Constraints:

mcqs.title: Recursion Defined Correctly
mcqs.description: In C++, a recursive function is best described as:
mcqs.Option1: A function that is called only once by main
mcqs.Option2: A function that calls itself, either directly or through another function
mcqs.Option3: A function declared with the static keyword
mcqs.Option4: A function that never returns a value

mcqs.title: Purpose of the Base Case
mcqs.description: What is the main job of the base case in a recursive function?
mcqs.Option1: It speeds up input and output
mcqs.Option2: It makes the function run at least twice
mcqs.Option3: It provides the stopping condition that ends the chain of recursive calls
mcqs.Option4: It allocates memory on the heap

mcqs.title: Cause of Infinite Recursion
mcqs.description: A recursive function never reaches its base case. What happens at run time?
mcqs.Option1: The calls repeat until the call stack runs out of memory and the program crashes
mcqs.Option3: The compiler refuses to build the program
mcqs.Option4: The function converts itself into a loop automatically

mcqs.title: Stack Frame per Call
mcqs.description: What does every single recursive call receive on the call stack?
mcqs.Option1: A shared single copy of all parameters
mcqs.Option2: Its own frame with its own copy of the parameters and local variables
mcqs.Option4: A fresh copy of the whole program

mcqs.title: Indirect Recursion Meaning
mcqs.description: Function A calls function B, and function B calls function A. This pattern is called:

mcqs.title: Tail Recursion at a Glance
mcqs.description: A recursive call qualifies as tail recursion when:
mcqs.Option1: It is the very last operation of the function, with nothing pending afterwards
mcqs.Option2: It happens inside a nested if block
mcqs.Option3: It passes more than one argument
mcqs.Option4: It calls at least two different functions

mcqs.title: Role of the Recursive Case
mcqs.description: The recursive case of a recursive function is the part that:
mcqs.Option4: Calls the same function again with a smaller or simpler input

mcqs.title: How Recursion Makes Progress
mcqs.description: For the recursion to terminate, every recursive call must:
mcqs.Option1: Work on a smaller or simpler input that moves towards the base case
mcqs.Option2: Use a bigger input than the previous call
mcqs.Option4: Return the same value it received

mcqs.title: Stack Overflow Warning Sign
mcqs.description: Which situation most strongly signals that a stack overflow may be approaching?
mcqs.Option1: The function uses long long instead of int
mcqs.Option2: The recursion depth keeps growing without a reachable base case
mcqs.Option4: The program prints many lines of output

mcqs.title: Unwinding Phase of Recursion
mcqs.description: After the base case returns, the pending work of earlier calls runs as frames pop off the stack. This phase is called:
mcqs.Option3: The unwinding phase, running from the most recent call back to the first
mcqs.Option4: The winding phase, running from the first call to the last

mcqs.title: Countdown Before the Call
mcqs.description: The function prints each number before making its recursive call. What does this program print?

mcqs.title: Sum Returned Through Frames
mcqs.description: The total is built while the call stack unwinds. What does this program print?

mcqs.title: Print Before and After the Call
mcqs.description: The function prints one line before diving and one line after returning. What is the exact output (one token per line, in order)?
mcqs.Option1: In2, In1, Dive, Out2, Out1 (in that order)
mcqs.Option2: In2, In1, Dive, Out1, Out2 (in that order)
mcqs.Option3: Dive, In2, In1, Out1, Out2 (in that order)
mcqs.Option4: In1, In2, Dive, Out1, Out2 (in that order)

mcqs.title: Fibonacci Function Value
mcqs.description: What does this program print?

mcqs.title: Missing Base Case Result
mcqs.description: A recursive factorial function forgets its base case entirely (the body only makes the recursive call). What happens at run time?
mcqs.Option2: The compiler inserts an implicit base case
mcqs.Option3: The calls keep stacking until the stack memory is exhausted and the program crashes
mcqs.Option4: The function silently returns an uninitialized value and the program continues normally

mcqs.title: Call Growth in Naive Fibonacci
mcqs.description: In the classic naive recursive fibonacci (fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2)), how does the total number of function calls behave as n grows?
mcqs.Option4: It grows roughly exponentially, because each call branches into two more calls that recompute the same subproblems

mcqs.title: Enter and Leave Trace
mcqs.description: The function logs entering each level and leaving each level. What is the exact output (one line per token, in order)?
mcqs.Option1: enter 2, enter 1, base, leave 2, leave 1 (in that order)
mcqs.Option2: enter 1, enter 2, base, leave 1, leave 2 (in that order)
mcqs.Option3: enter 2, enter 1, base, leave 1, leave 2 (in that order)
mcqs.Option4: base, enter 2, enter 1, leave 2, leave 1 (in that order)

mcqs.title: Reference Accumulator Result
mcqs.description: The accumulator is passed by reference, so every frame adds to the same variable. What does this program print?

mcqs.title: Nested Recursive Return Chain
mcqs.description: f calls itself and also calls the recursive helper g. What does this program print?

mcqs.title: Truth About Inline Functions
mcqs.description: Which statement about inline functions in C++ is correct?
mcqs.Option1: The inline keyword forces the compiler to expand every call, no matter how large the function body is
mcqs.Option2: Inline functions are pasted by the preprocessor like macros and skip type checking
mcqs.Option3: A recursive function must always be declared inline, otherwise it will not compile
mcqs.Option4: inline suggests expanding the body at the call site to save call overhead, but the compiler may ignore it, e.g. when the body is large or recursive
